items.name: Autonomous Build Slice
items.description: Run an approved feature slice autonomously from a preserved worktree through implementation, verification, PR creation, merge, and durable result reporting. The chain owns dirty-state preservation, worktree identity, checkpointing, runtime fallback, recovery handoff, and the canonical PR boundary.

items.name: Build Slice
items.description: Implement, devos-verify, and review a product slice in an isolated worktree. Assumes an approved spec exists; if tasks.md is missing, runs the required gap-analysis --dalio --fix gate on the spec, creates tasks, verifies planning, then proceeds into implementation. work-intake-preflight preserves existing dirty work before worktrees; worktrees is the first branch-isolation step and owns branch/worktree creation; downstream steps consume the returned workspace identity and actual path instead of deriving layout. checkpoint runs after worktrees to preserve workspace identity and actual path for mid-chain recovery. Refreshes the codebase map before implementation. audit-deps output feeds knowledge-pull; architecture-creator runs after both for current dependency context. commit --grouped --local-only captures every safe non-ignored worktree change before devos-code-review; files that should not be committed must be ignored or explicitly excluded before this step. A second commit --grouped --local-only runs after sync-completed-work so task-sync or review-fix dirtiness is not carried into create-pr or merge-feature. create-pr owns branch push, upstream setup, pull request creation/update, and readiness handoff. IMPORTANT: Worktree cleanup is automatic inside merge-feature after a successful full merge. Cleanup remains omitted from this chain because the chain schema has no conditional execution; merge-feature owns cleanup so failed merges and MVP merges do not destroy active work. Mirrored by skill: ~/.dev-os/.claude/skills/build-slice/SKILL.md

items.name: Cross-OS Skill Utilization and Vendoring Audit
items.description: Build an evidence-backed, approval-gated plan that audits global DevOS skills against every detected installable OS for activation, discoverability, command wiring, sync drift, skill quality, and justified vendoring opportunities.

skills.name: os-orchestrate
skills.args: --goal "Run the Cross-OS Skill Utilization and Vendoring Audit with scope_origin={scope_origin} and selected_os_packages={selected_os_packages} supplied by the chain runner. For explicit scope, accept canonical IDs from installed entries in the consuming root os-registry.yml, the consuming root manifest.json canonical source package, or immediate sibling *-os/manifest.json source packages, resolve each selected source path from that evidence, and audit only selected package skill source, profile, installed mirror, command, registry, telemetry, ownership, synchronization, and benchmark surfaces; for default-all scope preserve existing detection and report exact detected IDs. Treat global DevOS skill catalog reads as comparison-only. Missing 30-day activation telemetry is unknown with evidence provenance, never zero. Produce one aggregate report exposing scope_origin, requested_package_ids, resolved_package_ids, rejected_package_ids, selected_package_count, exact ordered selected IDs, zero-selected state, per-package evidence references and findings classified only as vendor, shared, OS-exclusive, improve-routing, keep-global, or retire. Revision 1 is strictly read-only: do not invoke mutating modes or write any selected or unselected OS package source, profile, mirror, command, registry, or skill content. Any non-empty remediation candidate set is a material revision 2, invalidates revision 1 approval, and requires a second explicit approval naming selected owners; route command work to commands-to-skills or bx-command-creator, skill quality/discoverability to bx-skill-creator, synchronization/vendoring to sync-skills, and ownership/registry defects to ownership-audit. Record producer-owned verification and unknown/failed outcomes; never mark remediation complete without it. Do not dispatch or route back to the cross-os-skill-audit chain."

parameters.name: --os
parameters.description: Limit the audit to one or more canonical OS package IDs; comma-separated values are accepted and normalized in first-seen order.
